requirements.subject: ent:set-type
requirements.canonical: A set type IS NOT compatible with any type other than a set type.
requirements.original: set types are only compatible with other set types and set of types are only compatible with other set of types.

requirements.subject: ent:set-of-type
requirements.canonical: A `set of` type IS NOT compatible with any type other than a `set of` type.
requirements.original: set types are only compatible with other set types and set of types are only compatible with other set of types.

requirements.subject: ent:set-type
requirements.canonical: The compatibility rules for record types SHALL apply to set types.
requirements.original: For set types the same compatibility rules shall apply as to record types and for set `of types the same` compatibility rules shall apply as to record `of types.`

requirements.subject: ent:set-of-type
requirements.canonical: The compatibility rules for `record of` types SHALL apply to `set of` types.
requirements.original: For set types the same compatibility rules shall apply as to record types and for set `of types the same` compatibility rules shall apply as to record `of types.`

requirements.subject: ent:set-type
requirements.canonical: When determining type compatibility of set types, the textual order of the fields in the set type definition IS decisive, although the order of elements at sending and receipt is unknown.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: This implies that though the order of elements at sending and receipt is unknown, when determining type compatibility for set types, the textual order of the fields in the type definition is decisive.

requirements.subject: ent:set-type
requirements.canonical: The arbitrary order of fields in a set value IS NOT relevant for type compatibility, because the field names identify which fields of the set type correspond to which set value fields.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: In set values the order of fields may be arbitrary, however this does not affect type compatibility as field names unambiguously identify, which fields of the related set type correspond to which set value fields.

requirements.subject: ent:union-value
requirements.canonical: A union value "b" of union type "B" IS compatible with union type "A" if the alternative selected in value "b" has a corresponding alternative with identical name in type "A" and the value of the selected alternative is compatible with the type of that corresponding alternative.
requirements.original: A union value "b" of union type "B" is compatible with union type "A" if the alternative selected in "b" has a corresponding alternative with identical name in "A" and the value of the selected alternative in "b" is compatible to the type of the corresponding alternative in "A".

requirements.subject: ent:union-value
requirements.condition: the first union compatibility rule did not determine compatibility
requirements.canonical: A union value "b" of union type "B" with a default alternative of type "C" IS compatible with an arbitrary type "A" if the alternative selected in value "b" is the default alternative and the value of the default alternative is compatible with type "A".
requirements.original: A union value "b" of union type "B" with a default alternative of type "C" is compatible with an arbitrary type "A" if the alternative selected in "b" is the default alternative and the value of the default alternative is compatible to "A".

requirements.subject: ent:value
requirements.condition: the first union compatibility rule did not determine compatibility
requirements.canonical: A value "a" of an arbitrary type "A" IS compatible with a union type "B" with a default alternative of type "C" if value "a" is compatible with type "C".
requirements.original: A value "a" of an arbitrary type "A" is compatible with a **union type "B" with a default alternative of type "C" if value "a" is compatible to "C".**

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: When checking the compatibility of two union types, a TTCN-3 tool SHALL first apply the rule based on identically named alternatives, which does not depend on a default alternative.
requirements.original: When considering the compatibility of two union types, initially the first rule (which is not dependent on the existence of a default alternative) shall be applied.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL use the default-alternative compatibility rules only if the rule based on identically named alternatives has not determined compatibility.
requirements.original: The second rule shall only be used to check compatibility, when - using the first rule - no compatibility has been determined.

ambiguity.issue: 'The second rule' is singular, but the 'Otherwise' bullet contains two default-alternative rules (union-to-arbitrary and arbitrary-to-union). Chose the reading that both are meant.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL use both default-alternative rules only if the identical-alternative rule has not determined compatibility.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL use only the union-to-arbitrary default-alternative rule as fallback; the arbitrary-to-union rule applies independently.

requirements.subject: ent:union-type
requirements.canonical: The prescribed order of the union compatibility rules IS intended to avoid ambiguity when a default alternative would also be compatible with the union type itself.
requirements.original: This order shall avoid ambiguity in case that a default alternative would otherwise also be compatible with the union itself.

requirements.subject: ent:union-type
requirements.canonical: A union type with a default alternative CAN be nested within another union type with a default alternative.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: It is possible to have nested unions with default alternatives.

requirements.subject: ent:union-type
requirements.canonical: Type compatibility along default alternatives IS transitive: the outermost union type is compatible with the type of the innermost default alternative if all containing alternatives are default alternatives.
requirements.original: The rules above make type compatibility along the default alternatives transitive, i.e. the outermost union type is compatible with the type of the innermost default union alternative if all containing alternatives are also default alternatives.

requirements.subject: ent:union-value
requirements.canonical: A union value with a default alternative used in an expression IS resolved to its long notation (the default alternative) before the expression is evaluated.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: When a union with a default alternative is used in an expression it will be resolved to its long notation, before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:union-value
requirements.canonical: A union value with a default alternative used directly in a `log` statement IS NOT converted to its default alternative; the union value itself is logged.
requirements.original: log(v_u4);  // results in "{ b:=true }" logged; for backward compatibility when a union value is used in a log statement directly, no conversion is performed.

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.canonical: An `anytype` type IS NOT compatible with any type other than an `anytype` type.
requirements.original: **anytype types are only compatible with other anytype types.

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.canonical: An `anytype` value "b" of `anytype` type "B" IS compatible with `anytype` type "A" if the alternative selected in value "b" is also contained in type "A".
requirements.original: An anytype value "b" of anytype type "B" is compatible** with anytype type "A" if the alternative selected in "b" is also contained in "A".

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.canonical: Only an `anytype` type that is constrained to a fixed set of types via list subtyping CAN cause `anytype` incompatibility, namely when the set of types contained in type "A" does not contain the type selected in value "b".
requirements.original: NOTE: Only anytype types that are constrained to a fixed set of types via list subtyping can be a potential cause for anytype incompatibility, i.e. if the set of types contained in type "A" does not contain the type selected in "b".

requirements.subject: ent:structured-type
requirements.canonical: The structured type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.2 ARE also valid for the sub-structures (fields and elements) of structured types.
requirements.original: The rules defined in this clause for structured types compatibility are also valid for the sub-structure of such types.

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: A value of any TTCN-3 type IS compatible with an open type occurring on the left hand side of an assignment.
requirements.original: Values of all existing TTCN-3 types are compatible with the open type occurring in the left hand side of an assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: A value of an open type occurring on the right hand side of an assignment IS compatible with type "A" if the actual value contained in the open type value is compatible with type "A".
requirements.original: Values of open type occurring on the right hand side of an assignment are compatible with a value "a" of a type "A", if the actual value contained in the open type value is compatible with "A".

ambiguity.issue: The rule says the open type value is compatible 'with a value "a" of a type "A"'; compatibility is defined between a value and a type, not between two values.

improper_terms.used: compatible with a value "a" of a type "A"

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.condition: a component reference is passed as actual parameter or assigned to a variable of a different component type
requirements.canonical: A component reference "b" of component type "B" IS compatible with component type "A" if all definitions of type "A" have identical definitions in type "B".
requirements.original: 1) Compatibility of a component reference value with a component type (e.g. when passing a component reference as an actual parameter to a function or an altstep or when assigning a component reference value to a variable of different component type): a component reference "b" of component type "B" is compatible with component type "A" if all definitions of "A" have identical definitions in "B".

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its `runs on` clause MAY be called or started on a component instance of type "B" if all definitions of type "A" have identical definitions in type "B".
requirements.original: 2) Runs on compatibility: a function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its runs on clause may be called or started on a component instance of type 'B' if all the definitions of "A" have identical definitions in "B".

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its `mtc` clause MAY be called or started in any context that has an `mtc` clause of type "B", or in a testcase with a `runs on` clause of type "B", if all port definitions of type "A" have identical definitions in type "B".
requirements.original: 3) Mtc compatibility: a function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its mtc clause may be called or started in any context that has a mtc clause of type "B" or a testcase with a runs on clause of type "B" if all the port definitions of "A" have identical definitions in "B".

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.condition: the type of the MTC is unknown in the calling function
requirements.canonical: If the type of the MTC is unknown in the calling function and component type "A" is not mtc-compatible with the type of the running MTC, a runtime error CAN occur.
requirements.original: If the type of the mtc is unknown in the calling function, this can lead to runtime errors if the component type "A" is not mtc-compatible with the type of the running mtc.

ambiguity.issue: 'can lead to runtime errors' does not say whether a runtime error is mandatory when incompatibility is detected.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL raise a runtime error when a function with an `mtc` clause of type "A" is called in a context whose running MTC is not mtc-compatible with "A".
A TTCN-3 tool MAY produce a runtime error (or undefined behaviour) in that situation.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its `system` clause MAY be called or started in any context that has a `system` clause of type "B", or in a testcase with a `runs on` clause of type "B" and no `system` clause, if all port definitions of type "A" have identical definitions in type "B".
requirements.original: 4) System compatibility: a function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its system clause may be called or started in any context that has a system clause of type "B" or a test case with a runs on clause of type "B" and no system clause if all the port definitions of "A" have identical definitions in "B".

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.condition: the type of the system is unknown in the calling function
requirements.canonical: If the type of the system is unknown in the calling function and component type "A" is not system-compatible with the type of the system the current test case was started on, a runtime error CAN occur.
requirements.original: If the type of the system is unknown in the calling function, this can lead to runtime errors if the component type "A" is not system-compatible with the type of the system the current test case was started on.

ambiguity.issue: 'can lead to runtime errors' does not say whether a runtime error is mandatory when incompatibility is detected.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL raise a runtime error when the system is not system-compatible with "A".
A TTCN-3 tool MAY produce a runtime error in that situation.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: For component type compatibility, a port instance in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical port types and identical identifiers.
requirements.original: a) For port instances, both the type and the identifier shall be identical.

requirements.subject: ent:timer
requirements.canonical: For component type compatibility, a timer instance in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical identifiers.
requirements.original: b) For timer instances, identifiers shall be identical and either both shall have identical initial durations or both shall have no initial duration.

requirements.subject: ent:timer
requirements.canonical: For component type compatibility, a timer instance in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL either both have identical initial durations or both have no initial duration.
requirements.original: b) For timer instances, identifiers shall be identical and either both shall have identical initial durations or both shall have no initial duration.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: For component type compatibility, a variable instance or constant definition in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical identifiers and identical types.
requirements.original: c) For variable instances and constant definitions, the identifiers, the types and initialization values shall be identical (in case of variables this means that either the values are missing in both definitions or are the same).

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: For component type compatibility, a variable instance or constant definition in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical initialization values; for variables, either both definitions have no initial value or both have the same value.
requirements.original: c) For variable instances and constant definitions, the identifiers, the types and initialization values shall be identical (in case of variables this means that either the values are missing in both definitions or are the same).

requirements.subject: ent:component-template
requirements.canonical: For component type compatibility, a component template in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical identifiers, types, formal parameter lists and assigned template or template field values.
requirements.original: d) For local template definitions, the identifiers, the types, the formal parameter lists and the assigned template or template field values shall be identical.

ambiguity.issue: 'local template definitions' means templates declared in the component type, which the glossary calls component templates.

non_requirement.reason: introduces the list of union compatibility rules extracted from 6.3.2.4-s002, s004, s005
'Otherwise' connector; the rule order is extracted from 6.3.2.4-s006 and s007, and the unit is cited as context of 6.3.2.4-004a/005a
introduces the four component type compatibility conditions extracted from 6.3.3-s002..s007
introduces the identity rules extracted from 6.3.3-s009..s012
